title: Conversational Tiling — mini PRD + experiments
content:
Quick summary

Problem: long-running conversational sessions are expensive because we repeatedly send and reprocess large context windows. We want a structure that (1) lets the model reuse semantically stable pieces of context across turns and sessions, (2) keeps the runtime and API ergonomics simple for client devs, and (3) enables efficient invalidation and explainability for retrieved context.

Idea: "conversational tiling" = break conversation state into small, named "tiles" (snippets) that are independently addressable, cacheable, and stitchable into a request. Tiles are semantic units (a task instruction, user profile facts, last few user messages on topic X, a decision summary) rather than raw token windows. Server and client coordinate on tile references instead of retransmitting full text.

Why might this help:
- Reduces per-request tokens (and cost) by replacing repeated content with short tile refs + signature.
- Faster kernel scheduling: common tiles can be prefetched / pinned to GPU memory or served from a fast in-memory cache.
- Better incremental updates: small edits only touch a tile version rather than reconstructing long context.
- UX affordance: UI could show tiles and let users pin, edit, or remove them (explainability/trust).

Core concepts / primitives

- Tile: minimal metadata = id, title (optional), short fingerprint/hash, semantic vectors (opt), size (tokens), created_at, last_used_at, trust_level. The body is the canonical text (or structured data).
- TileRef: lightweight reference included in requests: tile_id + version_hash + inclusion_hint (prefix/suffix/replace).
- TileCatalog: per-session or per-user index mapping high-level labels -> tile IDs (on the platform side).
- TilePolicy: TTLs, owner scope (session-only / user-global / org-shared), privacy flags, redaction rules.
- Stitching: runtime composes a request from client-provided TileRefs and ephemeral recent turns. We optionally expand tiles server-side to their bodies before sending to model.

Rough API sketch (server-backwards-compatible):
- create_tile (POST): {session_id?, scope, title?, text, metadata?} -> tile_id, version_hash
- list_tiles (GET): {session_id?, filters} -> [tile summaries]
- request: {model, tiles: [tileRef], recent: [turns], instructions} -> streaming response
- update_tile: patch text / bump version
- pin_tile / unpin_tile: control caching hints
- audit_tile: return provenance 

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Local developer flow: client SDK can create tiles and reference them in a standard generation call (no custom assembly on client).
- Savings: average tokens per generation reduced by >= 20% for multi-turn QA flows (internal benchmark)
- Latency: median first-byte latency for tile-heavy requests not > 10% relative to baseline on same model (prefetching used).
- Consistency: tile versioning prevents accidental use of stale context (tileRef with version must match tile version or request fails explicitly).

User stories / examples

1) Knowledge assistant: create tiles for "project brief", "requirements summary", "API contract". When user asks a question, client includes tileRefs for the project tiles plus the last 2 turns; model answers faster and uses less tokens.

2) Agent with tools: tool outputs can be summarized into "result tiles" and used as canonical memory for subsequent tool calls.

3) Personalization: user profile facts are stored in user-scoped tiles. Client opts-in to include them in requests for personalization.

Edge cases and risks

- Semantic drift: tiles might become stale or contradictory. Mitigation: versioning + explicit invalidation + automated refresh heuristics.
- Privacy/leakage: tiles may contain PII. Policy: tile scope and redaction at creation; support for KMS-wrapped tiles in Private mode.
- Exploding catalog: need GC and TTL; use LRU + pinned tiles to avoid unbounded memory.
- Developer complexity: too many primitives could confuse devs. Provide a simple default mode: server-side auto-tile suggestion + opaque tileRefs until they want control.

Experiments (quick validation path)

Experiment A: "turn dedupe" baseline
- Convert repeated user/system instructions in an internal multi-turn QA dataset into tiles (manual transform).
- Compare cost (tokens), P95 latency, and answer fidelity against same prompts w/o tiles.
- Target: 20% tokens saved, fidelity delta < 2% (measured by BLEU/ROUGE or task-specific metric).

Experiment B: "prefetch vs no-prefetch"
- Pin top N tiles for each session based on heuristics (recency + freq) and measure cold vs warm latency.
- Evaluate impact on GPU cache pressure and eviction.

Experiment C: end-user UX microtest
- Small internal cohort using a prototype UI that displays tiles as cards they can edit. Capture qualitative trust feedback and frequency of manual edit/delete.

Observability / metrics

- tokens_saved_per_request (derived)
- tiles_per_request distribution
- tile_hit_rate (when tileRef present, server expands rather than storing body in request)
- mean_time_to_first_byte (tile-heavy vs baseline)
- stale_tile_rate (attempts that reference tile version not found)
- user_edits_per_tile (proxy for drift / poor auto-tile generation)

Implementation notes / runtime considerations

- Server-side expansion: to maintain backward compatibility, if a request contains tileRefs the gateway resolves them and attaches the bodies to the prompt before calling the serving runtime. This keeps serving runtime unchanged initially.
- Long-term: move to a model-aware tile embed/retrieval layer: tiles kept in a short-lived KV cache with vector indexes for similarity matching to auto-suggest tiles.
- Caching: use a multi-tier cache: in-process small LRU, cluster-level pin pool (for dedicated pools), fallback to S3-like blob store.
- Security: per-tenant encryption keys for tile bodies in Private deployments.

Mock flow (developer):
1. client.create_tile(scope=user, text="My job: senior product manager at X, likes short answers") -> tile_abc123
2. client.generate({tiles:[{id:tile_abc123,version:sha1}], recent: [last_turns]})
3. server verifies version, expands tile body, constructs prompt: [tile-body] + [recent] + [instruction]
4. runtime returns streaming response

Open questions / TODOs
- UX: default naming and sizing heuristics for auto-created tiles (how long should a tile be?)
- Billing: do we bill tokens for expanded tile bodies? If so, need transparent per-tile token accounting in console.
- API ergonomics: should SDKs support local caching and offline tile editing?
- Eval: best objective metric for fidelity when content is split into tiles vs monolithic context?

Next steps (short term)
- Rapid prototype: gateway-level implementation that accepts tileRefs and expands them. (Assignee: Owen)
- Instrument a synthetic dataset to measure tokens saved on two internal products (search-assistant, code-assistant). (Assignee: Nora)
- UX sketch for tile card editor and onboarding copy (Assignee: Sam)
- Draft API surface and billing model proposal for review with product + finance by 2024-10-18.

Notes to self: keep the initial surface minimal (create/list/generate/pin). Aim for opt-in dev experience: auto-tiling behind a beta flag before making it a default. Capture developer confusion points in early usability sessions.

End.
